No wiring difference — stereotype is intent. @Service is prototype; @Component is singleton. @Component cannot be constructor-injected. @Service skips BeanDefinition registration. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (No wiring difference — stereotype is intent.) Q3: Third-party Jackson ObjectMapper as a bean? @Bean factory method on a @Configuration class. Put @Component on the library class in JDK. Only field injection into ObjectMapper works. Must subclass DispatcherServlet first. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (@Bean factory method on a @Configuration class.) Q4: Full @Configuration: @Bean a() { return x; } @Bean b() { return new B(a()); } a() call is intercepted — one X singleton. a() always runs twice creating two X. Illegal Java — methods cannot call methods. Forces request scope on both beans. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (a() call is intercepted — one X singleton.) Q5: @Profile("prod") bean missing in cluster. First check? spring.profiles.active / SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE. Whether the class is declared final only. GC collector choice in the Dockerfile. Whether HashMap load factor is 0.75. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (spring.profiles.active / SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE.) Q6: Default name of @Bean Clock utcClock()? utcClock — the method name. Clock — the return type always. clockConfig — the class name only. anonymous — beans cannot have names. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (utcClock — the method name.) 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 2 · Lesson 4 → · Cheat sheet

lessons.title: Properties, Conditions & Primary
lessons.text: 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 3 · Lesson 4 of 9 · Lesson 5 → · Cheat sheet Properties, @Conditional & @Primary ~35 minutes · Module 05 Lesson 4 of 9 · builds on S03 Senior Interview Focus: Spring decides whether a bean exists with conditions, and which bean wins with type matching, @Primary, and @Qualifier. Can you debug NoSuchBeanDefinitionException vs NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException in 30 seconds? Auto-config (S05) is this lesson applied at classpath scale. Primary sources: Externalized Configuration · Conditions (auto-config) · @Autowired 1. properties vs yml Same Environment . YAML is nested and lists; .properties is flat keys. Pick one per app. Illegal YAML indentation is a silent wrong-value bug — treat as a parse incident. 2. Property Sources (High Level) Boot builds an ordered Environment . Later sources win. Practical seniority: command line > env vars > profile-specific file > application.yml (simplified — full list is long; don’t recite 15 ranks unless asked). Env vars: SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL maps to spring.datasource.url . K8s ConfigMap/Secret → env → Environment. Never commit secrets (S08). 3. @Value public Pricing(@Value("${pricing.markup:1.0}") BigDecimal markup) { ... } Pros: one-off. Cons: stringly typed, scattered keys, SpEL #{ } surprises, hard to validate a group. Prefer for truly single flags. Nice to know: ${} is placeholder; #{} is SpEL — mixing them is a footgun. 4–6. @ConfigurationProperties @ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "shop.payments") public record PaymentsProps( @NotBlank String provider, Duration timeout ) {} Boot 3: records work. Enable with @EnableConfigurationProperties(PaymentsProps.class) or @ConfigurationPropertiesScan . Bind types, not strings. Validate with @Validated + Jakarta constraints — fail at startup, not on first payment. @Value @ConfigurationProperties Typing Per field conversion Structured object / record Validation Manual @Validated on the type IDE metadata Weak spring-boot-configuration-processor Use One key A config area (pool, payments, feature flags) 7. Profiles + Precedence Story application.yml markup: 1.0 application-prod.yml markup: 1.2 ENV SHOP_PAYMENTS_TIMEOUT=5s java -jar app.jar --shop.payments.provider=stripe Prod file overlays default; env overlays file; CLI wins. Interview: tell a story, not a 20-row table. 8–11. Conditions — Why a Bean Exists Must know: A Condition is evaluated against the ConditionContext (Environment, classloader, registry) before the bean is registered or created. False → no BeanDefinition (or skipped auto-config class). Annotation True when @Conditional Custom Condition.matches @ConditionalOnProperty Property equals expected (or present) @ConditionalOnClass Class on classpath (safe — uses class name string internally in auto-config) @ConditionalOnMissingBean No user bean of that type/name yet @ConditionalOnWebApplication Servlet or reactive web app type @Bean @ConditionalOnProperty(name = "shop.payments.provider", havingValue = "stripe") PaymentGateway stripeGateway(PaymentsProps props) { return new StripeGateway(props); } This is the seed of auto-config (S05): classpath + missing bean + property → create DataSource. 12–15. Multiple Beans Same Type Need PaymentGateway candidates: stripeGateway, razorpayGateway │ ├─ injection point has @Qualifier("stripeGateway") → that name ├─ field/param name matches bean name (fallback) ├─ @Primary on one candidate → that one └─ else NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException public interface PaymentGateway { Receipt charge(Money m); } @Service @Primary class StripePaymentService implements PaymentGateway { } @Service class RazorpayPaymentService implements PaymentGateway { } @Service class CheckoutService { CheckoutService( PaymentGateway defaultGw, // Stripe (@Primary) @Qualifier("razorpayPaymentService") PaymentGateway inrGw) { ... } } @Primary vs @Qualifier: Primary = default when type is unique-enough. Qualifier = this injection point wants a specific bean. Don’t use Primary as a silent override in a 6-implementations zoo — name them. 16. Startup Errors Exception Means Debug NoSuchBeanDefinitionException Zero candidates Scan (S03), profile, @Conditional* false, typo name NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException Two+ candidates, no winner @Primary / @Qualifier / inject List<T> Tools: --debug condition report (S05), /actuator/beans , /actuator/conditions (S08). Decision Tree Autowire type T 0 beans? → NoSuchBean → scan / profile / condition / @Bean 1 bean? → inject it 2+ beans? Qualifier / name match? → that bean @Primary unique? → primary else → NoUniqueBean Production Relevance Feature flags as @ConditionalOnProperty keep dead integrations off the classpath graph. A missing env var that should enable Stripe → NoSuchBean in prod only. Config validation at startup is cheaper than a 500 on checkout. Interview Articulation “Environment is an ordered set of property sources. I bind groups with @ConfigurationProperties and validate them. Conditions skip BeanDefinitions when a property or class is absent — that’s how auto-config backs off when I define my own DataSource. If two PaymentGateways exist, @Qualifier picks a site; @Primary picks the default; otherwise NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException.” Senior Interview Questions @Value vs @ConfigurationProperties — when each? How does an env var become spring.datasource.url? What does @ConditionalOnMissingBean actually check? Walk two PaymentGateway beans into CheckoutService. @Primary vs @Qualifier — conflict if both present? NoSuchBean vs NoUniqueBean — first three checks each. Why validate properties at startup? How do conditions preview auto-configuration? Revision Notes Environment overlay: files → env → CLI (simplified). Records + @ConfigurationProperties + @Validated. Conditions gate registration. Resolution: qualifier → primary → fail. Interview One-Liners “Zero beans is scan/condition; many beans is identity.” “@Primary is a default, not a substitute for naming.” “Fail at refresh() if config is illegal.” Senior MCQs Q1: Two PaymentGateway beans, no @Primary/@Qualifier? NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException at injection. Spring randomly picks one each request. Both are silently ignored forever. Tomcat converts them into filters. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException at injection.) Q2: @ConditionalOnProperty false. Result? Bean is not registered / not created. Bean is created then immediately destroyed. Bean becomes request-scoped automatically. Only field injection still works. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Bean is not registered / not created.) Q3: Prefer @ConfigurationProperties when? A group of related typed settings. You need SpEL inside SQL strings. The value is a local loop counter. You want to skip the Environment. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (A group of related typed settings.) Q4: @Qualifier vs @Primary at one injection point? Qualifier wins for that parameter. Primary always overrides Qualifier. Both are ignored if types match. Causes Metaspace leaks in JDK 21. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Qualifier wins for that parameter.) Q5: NoSuchBeanDefinitionException first checks? Scan path, profile, conditions, bean name. Only whether Tomcat maxThreads is 200. Whether the class used synchronized. G1 vs ZGC collector selection only. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Scan path, profile, conditions, bean name.) Q6: @ConditionalOnMissingBean purpose in Boot? User @Bean makes auto-config back off. Deletes all beans of other types. Forces field injection on DataSource. Disables the Environment completely. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (User @Bean makes auto-config back off.) 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 3 · Lesson 5 → · Cheat sheet

lessons.title: Auto-Configuration Internals
lessons.text: 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 4 · Lesson 5 of 9 · Lesson 6 → · Cheat sheet Spring Boot Auto-Configuration Internals ~40 minutes · Module 05 Lesson 5 of 9 · deepest theory lesson · builds on S04 , classloaders / fat JAR Senior Interview Focus: Auto-config is not magic. It is: classpath entries listed in AutoConfiguration.imports + @Conditional* + “back off if user already defined the bean.” Can you answer “why did this DataSource appear?” and “why didn’t it?” with --debug / Condition Evaluation Report? Primary sources: Using Auto-configuration · Creating Auto-configuration · Boot 3 — imports file 1–2. Why Auto-Config Exists; Framework vs Boot Spring Framework: IoC, MVC, AOP, tx — you wire or scan your classes. Spring Boot: opinions + starters + embedded server + auto-configuration : if JDBC is on the classpath and you did not define a DataSource, Boot creates one from spring.datasource.* . Goal: 80% of apps share the same 50 @Bean methods. Encode them once. Let conditions skip the rest. 3. @SpringBootApplication — Three Meta-Annotations @SpringBootApplication = @SpringBootConfiguration → @Configuration (your app config) + @EnableAutoConfiguration → import auto-config classes (this lesson) + @ComponentScan → your package tree (S03) You can split them. Almost nobody does. Know the split for interviews. 4–5. What @EnableAutoConfiguration Triggers @EnableAutoConfiguration │ ▼ AutoConfigurationImportSelector │ reads from every JAR on the classpath: ▼ META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports │ one FQCN per line ▼ Candidate auto-config classes (filtered by conditions + exclude) │ ▼ Imported as BeanDefinitions (lite @AutoConfiguration, proxyBeanMethods=false) Must know (Boot 3): Auto-config registration is the imports file. META-INF/spring.factories key EnableAutoConfiguration was removed in 3.0. Other spring.factories keys still exist. Interviewers still say “spring.factories” — correct them politely: “for auto-config, imports file since 2.7/3.0.” Fat JAR: Boot’s nested loader ( LaunchedURLClassLoader ) still exposes those META-INF files from nested jars. 6. Anatomy of an Auto-Config Class @AutoConfiguration @ConditionalOnClass(DataSource.class) @EnableConfigurationProperties(DataSourceProperties.class) @Import(DataSourcePoolMetadataProvidersConfiguration.class) public class DataSourceAutoConfiguration { // nested @Configuration classes with more @ConditionalOn* } @AutoConfiguration — stereotype; can declare before / after other auto-configs (ordering). Must not be component-scanned. Only loaded via the imports file. Inner beans typically @ConditionalOnMissingBean(DataSource.class) . 7–8. Conditions Deep Dive + JDBC Story Need a DataSource bean? │ ├─ spring-jdbc / DataSource class on classpath? @ConditionalOnClass ├─ User already defined DataSource? @ConditionalOnMissingBean → SKIP ├─ spring.datasource.url (or embedded DB) present? └─ Web vs none — sometimes extra conditions │ ▼ Hikari DataSource bean created Add spring-boot-starter-data-jpa → Hibernate + DataSource auto-config light up. Remove the starter → conditions fail → beans gone. Classpath-driven behavior. 9–11. Convention, Risk, Back-off Benefit: empty app + starter-web = Tomcat + DispatcherServlet. Risk: surprise beans (Redis connection to localhost in prod because starter-data-redis sneaked in). Always know your dependency tree. Back-off (must know): you declare @Bean DataSource myDs() → @ConditionalOnMissingBean(DataSource.class) is false → Hikari auto-config does not create a second pool. Your bean wins. 12. Exclude @SpringBootApplication(exclude = DataSourceAutoConfiguration.class) public class ShopApplication { } Or spring.autoconfigure.exclude=... . Use when you must not have a DataSource (library, batch with custom routing) and conditions aren’t enough. 13. Debugging Workflow java -jar app.jar --debug (or logging.level.org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure=DEBUG ) Read Condition Evaluation Report — Positive matches vs Negative matches with the failing condition named Actuator /actuator/conditions (S08) in a secured management port /actuator/beans — is the bean in the factory at all? Must know: the report names the condition class that failed — e.g. OnClassCondition , OnBeanCondition . That is the mechanism. Not “Spring decided not to.” 14. Scenario: “Why did Spring create this bean?” Trace: which starter brought which auto-config class → which condition was true → which @Bean method. Example: Hikari because DataSourceAutoConfiguration matched and you set spring.datasource.url . 15. Scenario: “Why didn’t Spring create this bean?” Negative match. Typical: class missing (forgot starter), OnMissingBean lost (you already defined one), property matchIfMissing=false and key absent, exclude , wrong web application type (servlet vs reactive — S09). 16. Tiny Custom Auto-Config (Illustrative) my-starter.jar META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports com.acme.MeowAutoConfiguration @AutoConfiguration @ConditionalOnClass(CatClient.class) class MeowAutoConfiguration { @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean CatClient catClient() { return new CatClient(); } } Not a starter-authoring course. Enough to know libraries ship this file — not @ComponentScan of the library. Mental Model dependency on classpath + AutoConfiguration.imports lists a class + @Conditional* all true + @ConditionalOnMissingBean still true = bean appears Auto-config ≠ magic. Misconceptions “Boot scans all JARs for @Component.” Libraries should not. Auto-config is explicit imports. “spring.factories still registers auto-config on Boot 3.” No. “I cannot override Boot beans.” You can — MissingBean pattern, or exclude. Production Relevance Unexpected Mongo client in a service that only needed a driver transitively — extra connections, extra failure modes. Review mvn dependency:tree like you review BeanDefinitions. Fat JAR classloader still participates (JVM S06). Interview Articulation “@EnableAutoConfiguration loads classes listed in AutoConfiguration.imports on the classpath. Each class is a bundle of conditional @Bean methods. If I already define a DataSource, OnMissingBean is false and Boot backs off. I debug with the Condition Evaluation Report from --debug or /actuator/conditions, not by guessing.” Senior Interview Questions Three meta-annotations on @SpringBootApplication. Boot 3 discovery file vs spring.factories. Why must auto-config classes not be component-scanned? Walk DataSource creation conditions. How does a user @Bean disable Hikari auto-config? How do you exclude DataSourceAutoConfiguration? What does --debug print that /beans does not? Classpath adds redis starter — what mechanism creates RedisConnectionFactory? servlet vs reactive OnWebApplication — why would MVC beans vanish? proxyBeanMethods false on @AutoConfiguration — implication? Revision Notes imports file → candidates → conditions → beans. OnMissingBean = user override hook. exclude = sledgehammer. --debug / conditions endpoint = source of truth. Interview One-Liners “A starter is a POM plus auto-config, not a runtime daemon.” “Negative matches are the answer key.” “My DataSource bean is the feature, not a fight with Boot.” Senior MCQs Q1: Boot 3 auto-config class names live in? AutoConfiguration.imports under META-INF/spring. Only web.xml in the WAR root. The module-info.java provides list. JDK META-INF/services of java.sql. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (AutoConfiguration.imports under META-INF/spring.) Q2: User defines @Bean DataSource. Hikari auto-config? Backs off via @ConditionalOnMissingBean. Always creates a second pool anyway. Deletes the user bean at runtime. Promotes DataSource to request scope. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Backs off via @ConditionalOnMissingBean.) Q3: @SpringBootApplication does not include? @EnableAspectJAutoProxy by default here. @SpringBootConfiguration alias. @EnableAutoConfiguration trigger. @ComponentScan of the app package. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (@EnableAspectJAutoProxy by default here.) The three are Configuration + EnableAutoConfiguration + ComponentScan. AOP is separate (S06), though Boot enables proxying when needed. Q4: Best tool for “why wasn’t X auto-configured?” Condition Evaluation Report (--debug). Only jmap histogram of the heap. HashMap load factor in the JDK. Replacing all beans with enums. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Condition Evaluation Report (--debug).) Q5: spring.factories EnableAutoConfiguration key on Boot 3? Removed for auto-config registration. The only supported discovery mechanism. Required alongside Tomcat XML. Used only by WebFlux Netty. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Removed for auto-config registration.) Q6: Auto-config classes should be? Listed in imports — never component-scanned. Annotated @RestController in default package. Loaded by Thread.currentThread only. Compiled without -parameters always. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Listed in imports — never component-scanned.) Q7: Adding starter-data-redis suddenly creates a factory. Why? Classpath + imports + matching conditions. JVM JIT inlined Redis into Tomcat. @Primary on Object always includes Redis. GC created it as a safepoint side effect. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Classpath + imports + matching conditions.) Q8: exclude = DataSourceAutoConfiguration.class means? That auto-config class is not imported. JDBC driver is deleted from the JDK. All @Repository beans become prototypes. Actuator health is forced down. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (That auto-config class is not imported.) 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 4 · Lesson 6 → · Cheat sheet

lessons.title: AOP Proxies & @Transactional
lessons.text: 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 5 · Lesson 6 of 9 · Lesson 7 → · Cheat sheet AOP Proxies, JDK vs CGLIB & @Transactional Internals ~40 minutes · Module 05 Lesson 6 of 9 · critical interview lesson · builds on this/super , lifecycle / BPP Senior Interview Focus: @Transactional does nothing unless the call enters the Spring proxy . Self-invocation this.save() skips the proxy — same trap as this.txMethod() in oop-0013 . Can you draw Caller → Proxy → advice → target, pick JDK vs CGLIB, and explain REQUIRED vs REQUIRES_NEW without hand-waving “Spring handles it”? Primary sources: Proxying Mechanisms · Transaction Management · Understanding the Spring Framework’s Declarative Transaction Implementation 1. Why Proxies Cross-cutting: transactions, security, metrics. Keep them off the domain method body. Mechanism: wrap the bean with a proxy that runs advice then delegates to the target . Spring AOP is proxy-based (runtime). Full AspectJ compile/load-time weaving is out of scope. 2. Vocabulary Term Meaning Target Your real OrderService instance Proxy Object the container injects into other beans Advice Code around the call (begin tx, log, …) Join point A method execution (Spring AOP limitation) Pointcut Which methods get advice ( @Transactional is a shortcut) 3. Call Chain Caller (Controller) │ orderService.place(cmd) // reference is the PROXY ▼ ┌──────────── Spring Proxy ────────────┐ │ TransactionInterceptor (advice) │ │ begin / get tx │ │ │ │ │ ▼ │ │ target.place(cmd) │ │ │ │ │ commit / rollback │ └──────────────────────────────────────┘ BeanPostProcessor ( AbstractAutoProxyCreator ) replaces the bean with the proxy after init (S02 after-BPP). Other beans receive the proxy reference. 4–6. JDK vs CGLIB JDK dynamic proxy CGLIB subclass How java.lang.reflect.Proxy implementing interfaces Runtime subclass of the target class Needs Target implements an interface; callers use the interface Non-final class; intercept non-final public methods Framework default If ≥1 interface → JDK If no interface → CGLIB Boot default spring.aop.proxy-target-class=true → CGLIB even with interfaces Must know: Spring Framework docs: interface → JDK. Spring Boot sets class proxies on by default so injecting the concrete class still hits the proxy. If you inject by interface only, both work. Mixing “I injected the class” + proxy-target-class=false → ClassCastException. CGLIB proxy is created via Objenesis — constructor of the subclass is not a second business ctor call in normal JVMs. 7. final — Proxy Limits Final class: CGLIB cannot subclass → proxy creation fails for class-based proxy. Final method: CGLIB cannot override → no advice on that method (silent skip — deadly for @Transactional). Private methods: never proxied. Package-private: unreliable across classloaders. 8–9. @Transactional Internals enter proxy method │ ▼ PlatformTransactionManager.getTransaction(def) │ REQUIRED: join existing or begin new ▼ target method │ ├─ return normally → commit ├─ RuntimeException / Error → rollback (default) └─ checked Exception → commit unless rollbackFor=... Default rollback: unchecked only. throws Exception that you catch-and-wrap as checked → commit unless rollbackFor = Exception.class . Must know. Swallowed exception ( catch (RuntimeException e) { log } without rethrow) → interceptor sees success → commit . 10. Propagation (Interview Pair) Propagation If tx exists If none REQUIRED (default) Join it Begin one REQUIRES_NEW Suspend, begin nested independent tx, resume Begin one REQUIRES_NEW: audit log that must save even if outer tx rolls back. Cost: extra connection, deadlock risk. Do not sprinkle. Nice to know: NESTED uses savepoints (JDBC). NEVER / NOT_SUPPORTED / MANDATORY — name them if asked; don’t invent. 11. Transaction Boundaries The boundary is the proxy method you entered. Repository calls inside that method join REQUIRED. HTTP filter is outside. @Transactional on controller works but is a smell (transaction includes JSON mapping). Prefer service layer. Reactive @Transactional is a different stack (S09 caveat: WebFlux + blocking @Transactional on servlet model ≠ event-loop safe). 12–13. Self-Invocation OrderService (target) place() // no @Transactional this.charge() // SAME this — no proxy — no tx @Transactional charge() Caller → proxy.place() → target.place() → this.charge() never re-enters proxy. You studied this bypassing Spring AOP in this & super . Fix: move charge to another bean (self-injection of the proxy, or TransactionTemplate ). Not AopContext.currentProxy() in app code. Controller → proxy.place() // tx if @Transactional on place OtherService → orderService.charge() // goes through proxy ✓ 14. Pitfall Checklist (@Transactional doesn’t work) Self-invocation / same class Method not public (or final + CGLIB) Bean not Spring-managed ( new OrderService() ) Checked exception / swallowed exception Called from another thread without passing context (tx is thread-bound — thread ) Wrong DataSource / no PlatformTransactionManager bean Long tx holding DB connections → pool exhaustion (S07) 15. readOnly = true Hint to the manager / Hibernate flush skip. Not a hard SQL write ban. A save() inside readOnly may still write depending on provider. Don’t use it as security. 16. Realistic Sketch @Service public class OrderService { private final OrderRepository repo; private final PaymentGateway gateway; public OrderService(OrderRepository repo, PaymentGateway gateway) { this.repo = repo; this.gateway = gateway; } @Transactional public OrderId place(PlaceOrder cmd) { Order order = repo.save(Order.from(cmd)); gateway.charge(order.total()); // if this throws RuntimeException → rollback save return order.id(); } } Controller injects OrderService (proxy). One HTTP thread, one tx, one rollback story. Production Relevance Silent commit after caught exceptions. Self-invocation in “refactor extract method.” Final methods on @Transactional services after a record conversion. REQUIRES_NEW leaking connections under load. Interview Articulation “Declarative transactions are Spring AOP. The container injects a proxy; advice starts a transaction via PlatformTransactionManager, invokes the target, then commits or rolls back. Default rollback is runtime exceptions. this.foo() never hits the proxy, so @Transactional on foo is skipped. Boot class-proxies with CGLIB unless you turn that off; final methods then silently lose advice.” Senior Interview Questions Draw the proxy call chain for @Transactional. JDK vs CGLIB — Framework vs Boot default. Why final methods break transactions. Self-invocation: exact this reference story. Checked vs runtime rollback defaults. REQUIRED vs REQUIRES_NEW with a failure in the inner method. Where should the tx boundary live? Transaction + thread pools — is context inherited? readOnly=true — what it is not. Debug checklist when “tx doesn’t roll back.” Revision Notes Advice runs only through the proxy. Boot: CGLIB class proxy default. Rollback: RuntimeException; set rollbackFor for checked. REQUIRED join; REQUIRES_NEW suspend+new. this.method() bypass; other bean OK. Interview One-Liners “If the call never entered the proxy, there was no transaction.” “Catch without rethrow is a commit.” “REQUIRES_NEW is a new connection story, not a flag of quality.” Senior MCQs Q1: this.save() inside the same @Service? Bypasses the proxy — no @Transactional advice. Always starts REQUIRES_NEW automatically. CGLIB rewrites this to the proxy always. Fails compilation on Java 21. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Bypasses the proxy — no @Transactional advice.) Q2: Default rollback for throws Exception (checked)? Commit unless rollbackFor includes it. Always rollback like RuntimeException. Tomcat converts it to HTTP 204. Opens a second nested savepoint always. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Commit unless rollbackFor includes it.) Q3: Spring Boot AOP proxy default? Class-based CGLIB (proxy-target-class true). JDK proxies only, even without interfaces. No proxies — bytecode weaving required. Enum singletons replace all proxies. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Class-based CGLIB (proxy-target-class true).) Q4: REQUIRED when a tx already exists? Join the existing transaction. Always suspend and start another. Ignore @Transactional completely. Bind the tx to a new virtual thread. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Join the existing transaction.) Q5: final @Transactional method on a CGLIB proxy? Advice typically does not run. JDK proxy is used instead automatically. JVM rejects the class at verify time. readOnly becomes a hard SQL lock. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Advice typically does not run.) Q6: Catch RuntimeException, log, no rethrow? Interceptor commits — exception was swallowed. Rollback still happens via ThreadLocal. REQUIRES_NEW starts on the catch block. Actuator marks liveness DOWN. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Interceptor commits — exception was swallowed.) Q7: new OrderService(repo) inside a controller? Not a bean — no transactional proxy. Boot wraps every new automatically. Equals injecting the singleton proxy. Forces request scope on the repo. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Not a bean — no transactional proxy.) Q8: readOnly = true guarantees? A hint — not a hard write block. Database user is switched to SELECT. CGLIB cannot proxy the class. Propagation becomes NEVER always. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (A hint — not a hard write block.) 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 5 · Lesson 7 → · Cheat sheet

lessons.title: Servlet Stack: Tomcat, Filters & MVC
lessons.text: 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 6 · Lesson 7 of 9 · Lesson 8 → · Cheat sheet Servlet Stack: Tomcat, Filters & MVC Dispatch ~35 minutes · Module 05 Lesson 7 of 9 · builds on threads , pools , virtual threads Senior Interview Focus: One HTTP request occupies a Tomcat worker for the whole blocking JDBC call. Can you walk Client → Tomcat → Filter → DispatcherServlet → Controller → Service, name where a correlation ID is set, and diagnose 200 Tomcat threads vs 20 Hikari connections? This is production, not servlet certification. Primary sources: DispatcherServlet · Boot Servlet Web · Graceful Shutdown Mental Model — Request Path Client → Load balancer → Embedded Tomcat connector │ ▼ Tomcat worker thread (or virtual thread if enabled) │ ▼ Servlet Filter chain (security, CORS, MDC) │ ▼ DispatcherServlet │ ├─ HandlerMapping → @RequestMapping match ├─ HandlerAdapter → invoke controller ├─ Controller → args, HttpMessageConverter ├─ Service / @Transactional proxy (S06) └─ Repository → JDBC (thread still blocked) │ ▼ return → converters → filters → client 1. Embedded Tomcat in Boot starter-web pulls Tomcat. Boot creates a TomcatServletWebServerFactory , starts a connector on server.port (8080). No external catalina install. The JVM process is the server ( JVM S01 ). You can switch to Jetty/Undertow via starters. Same servlet programming model. 2. Platform / Request Threads Classic: pool of platform threads ( server.tomcat.threads.max , default 200). Each in-flight blocking request holds one thread. You sized pools in Executors — same math: threads ≈ concurrent blocking work, not QPS. Boot 3.2+: spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true — Tomcat can run requests on virtual threads ( VT ). Helps blocking I/O . Does not help CPU-bound work. Pinning still applies ( synchronized , native). 3. Connector (Practical) Acceptor takes the TCP connection; worker runs the servlet. Timeouts: connection, keep-alive. You rarely tune protocol internals in interviews — you tune max threads , accept count , and downstream pools . 4. Servlet Filter Chain Filters wrap the servlet. Ordered ( @Order / FilterRegistrationBean ). Typical: correlation ID into MDC, security, metrics. @Component public class CorrelationFilter extends OncePerRequestFilter { @Override protected void doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, FilterChain chain) throws ServletException, IOException { String cid = Optional.ofNullable(req.getHeader("X-Correlation-Id")) .orElse(UUID.randomUUID().toString()); MDC.put("cid", cid); try { chain.doFilter(req, res); } finally { MDC.clear(); // ThreadLocal leak otherwise — JVM S06 / concurrency } } } Must know: MDC is ThreadLocal. Forget clear() on a pool thread → leaked IDs (and classloader leaks on redeploy). Virtual threads: still clear; cheaper threads ≠ optional hygiene. 5–8. DispatcherServlet & MVC DispatcherServlet — front controller. One servlet mapping / . HandlerMapping — path + method + consumes → handler method. HandlerAdapter — invokes that method (you don’t call it). Argument resolvers — @RequestBody , @PathVariable , Principal. HttpMessageConverter — JSON via Jackson, etc. 404 vs 405 vs 415: mapping miss vs method vs media type — interview precision. 9. @ControllerAdvice Exception → HTTP mapping in one place. After the controller throws, before the response is committed. Not a substitute for Filter errors that never reach the dispatcher. 10–12. Blocking Path & Exhaustion Tomcat max = 200 Hikari max = 20 Inbound: 200 slow queries 20 threads: in JDBC (have a connection) 180 threads: blocked waiting on Hikari pool Cost: 180 platform stacks + timeouts + tail latency Thread dump: socketRead0 / HikariProxyConnection.getConnection (JVM S08) Must know: Fix the bottleneck (query, pool size vs DB, timeouts). Raising Tomcat to 2000 without DB capacity makes GC and context switching worse. Virtual threads: waiting on Hikari still serializes on 20 connections. VT does not multiply database capacity. 13. Filter vs HandlerInterceptor vs @ControllerAdvice Filter HandlerInterceptor @ControllerAdvice Layer Servlet Spring MVC MVC exception / binding Sees All requests to the servlet Mapped handlers (not raw static if bypassed) Controller exceptions Use Auth gateway, CID, CORS Handler-specific metrics, model API error JSON Spring Security is a filter chain — out of scope for internals here; know it sits before DispatcherServlet. 14. Correlation ID Propagate X-Correlation-Id to downstream HTTP and logs. Actuator/metrics tags later (S08). Without it, six replicas are a haystack. Production Relevance Latency spike: thread dump + Hikari metrics, not “restart Tomcat.” Graceful shutdown: Boot waits in-flight requests ( server.shutdown=graceful ) — K8s preStop should match. Interview Articulation “Embedded Tomcat runs the servlet container in-process. A worker thread (or virtual thread) runs the filter chain then DispatcherServlet, which maps to a controller. If the service blocks on JDBC, that thread stays occupied. I size Tomcat against downstream pools. Exhausted Tomcat with idle CPU often means all workers are blocked on I/O — dump threads, don’t add replicas blindly.” Senior Interview Questions Walk an HTTP GET from NIC to repository. Default Tomcat max threads — what does 200 mean? Filter vs Interceptor vs ControllerAdvice. Why MDC.clear in finally? 200 Tomcat / 20 Hikari under load — dump what? When do virtual threads help this stack? What does DispatcherServlet do that Tomcat does not? 404 vs 405 vs 415. Revision Notes Worker thread held for entire blocking request. DispatcherServlet = front controller. Filters wrap servlet; interceptors wrap handlers. Pool mismatch: Tomcat vs Hikari vs DB. VT: more waiters, same DB capacity. Interview One-Liners “The servlet thread is the currency of a blocking API.” “Hikari is often the real max concurrency.” “MDC without finally is a lie in the next request.” Senior MCQs Q1: Blocking JDBC inside a controller. Worker thread? Stays occupied until the query returns. Returns to the pool during socket read. Is always a virtual thread in Boot 2.7. Migrates to the common ForkJoinPool. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Stays occupied until the query returns.) Q2: DispatcherServlet role? Front controller: map and invoke handlers. The JDBC driver wrapper for Hikari. The JVM safepoint coordinator. Kubernetes liveness HTTP client. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Front controller: map and invoke handlers.) Q3: Correlation ID in a Filter. Must also? Clear MDC in finally on the worker. Store it in a static HashMap only. Disable Tomcat to avoid ThreadLocal. Put it in Metaspace as a class constant. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Clear MDC in finally on the worker.) Q4: 200 busy Tomcat threads, Hikari 20. Likely? Threads waiting on the DB pool. Need 200 more database replicas first. DispatcherServlet is not registered. Only GC safepoints can explain it. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Threads waiting on the DB pool.) Q5: spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true helps most? Many concurrent blocking I/O requests. Single-thread CPU-bound JSON crypto. Replacing Hikari with unbounded queues. Avoiding all proxy transactional advice. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Many concurrent blocking I/O requests.) Q6: HandlerInterceptor vs Filter? Interceptor is MVC; Filter is servlet API. Filter only runs after @ControllerAdvice. Interceptor replaces Tomcat connectors. They are identical JVM bytecodes. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Interceptor is MVC; Filter is servlet API.) 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 6 · Lesson 8 → · Cheat sheet

lessons.title: Actuator, Health & Metrics
lessons.text: 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 7 · Lesson 8 of 9 · Lesson 9 → · Cheat sheet Actuator, Health, Metrics & Production Configuration ~30 minutes · Module 05 Lesson 8 of 9 · builds on JVM diagnostics , conditions Senior Interview Focus: Observability is how you keep a JVM service honest in K8s. Can you map liveness vs readiness to probes, name which Actuator endpoint you hit first on a latency spike, and say what must never be public? Actuator is the app view; jcmd/JFR is the JVM view — both. Primary sources: Spring Boot Actuator · Endpoints · Metrics 1–2. Why Observability; What Actuator Is Without signals you guess. Actuator exposes HTTP/JMX endpoints and wires Micrometer meters. It is a Boot feature (auto-config), not a replacement for logs or traces. 3. Endpoints (What Each Is For) Endpoint Question it answers /health Should this instance take traffic / is process alive? /info Build version, git commit — deploy verification /metrics Named meters (JVM, Tomcat, Hikari, HTTP) /loggers Runtime log level (dangerous if public) /threaddump Same idea as jstack — app-level dump /heapdump hprof — huge, sensitive, last resort /conditions Auto-config report (S05) /beans /env /configprops Wiring and property values — secrets risk 4. Exposure — Never Public Full Actuator Must know: By default web exposure is limited ( health often). Do not include=* on the public 8080. Pattern: management.server.port=8081 — not on the LoadBalancer NetworkPolicy: only kubelet / Prometheus scrape Auth on sensitive endpoints if the port is reachable /env and /heapdump on the internet = incident. 5–7. Health, Liveness, Readiness, K8s Liveness → kubelet: restart the container if deadlocked / stuck Readiness → Service: remove from LB if cannot accept traffic (warming, downstream down) Boot 2.3+: /health/liveness and /health/readiness (or groups). Custom HealthIndicator for “can I reach Redis?” — usually readiness , not liveness (don’t restart-loop because Redis blipped). Trap: liveness pinging the database → DB outage = crashloop. Liveness = process health. Readiness = dependency health. 8–10. Micrometer Meters (counters, timers, gauges) → registry (Prometheus, OTLP, …). You don’t implement scrape format by hand. Metrics that matter: HTTP latency / error rate (server requests) JVM memory, GC pause (ties Module 04) Tomcat threads busy / max Hikari: active, pending, timeout @Timed("checkout.place") public OrderId place(PlaceOrder cmd) { ... } // or registry.counter("payments.failed", "provider", "stripe").increment(); Nice to know: Cardinality explosion (per-user tags) kills Prometheus. Tag bounded sets only. 11–12. Production Config & Secrets Profiles: prod in the cluster only Env vars / K8s Secret / Vault — not git Externalized config (S04) — 12-factor 13. Incident: Latency Spike — First Moves 1. HTTP metrics: p99, error ratio, in-flight 2. Hikari pending / Tomcat busy → pool story (S07) 3. /threaddump or jcmd Thread.print → BLOCKED vs socketRead (JVM S08) 4. GC metrics — if CPU in GC, Module 04 path 5. Do not heapdump first on a giant heap under load 14. Actuator vs jcmd Actuator: needs HTTP, security, may miss native deadlocks if the web thread pool is stuck. jcmd from the pod: works if the JVM still answers attach. Seniors use both. Production Relevance Probes misconfigured = rolling deploy never becomes Ready, or pods killed during GC pause (liveness timeout too aggressive). Heapdump endpoint left open = PII on the internet. Interview Articulation “Actuator exposes health and metrics. Liveness is ‘restart me’; readiness is ‘stop sending traffic.’ I scrape Micrometer via a private management port. On latency I look at HTTP timers, thread and connection pool gauges, then a thread dump. Heapdump and /env stay locked down. JVM tools remain valid when HTTP is already dead.” Senior Interview Questions Liveness vs readiness — K8s mapping. Why not check DB on liveness? Which endpoints must not be public? Latency spike — first three signals. Micrometer vs logging vs tracing. When Actuator dump vs jcmd? Custom HealthIndicator — which group? How secrets get into Environment in K8s. Revision Notes Management port + least exposure. Liveness ≠ dependencies. Hikari + Tomcat + HTTP timers. Conditions endpoint debugs S05. Actuator + jcmd complementary. Interview One-Liners “Restart loops from a DB health check are a liveness mistake.” “include=* on 8080 is a finding, not a convenience.” “Metrics first, dumps second, heapdump last.” Senior MCQs Q1: Redis down. Which probe should fail? Readiness — stop traffic, don’t crashloop. Liveness — kubelet must always restart. Neither — hide all health endpoints. Only heapdump should turn red. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Readiness — stop traffic, don’t crashloop.) Q2: Safe public exposure? Minimal health — never env/heapdump on 8080. include=* on the LoadBalancer port. /loggers open without auth globally. /beans to the whole internet always. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Minimal health — never env/heapdump on 8080.) Q3: First metric family on API latency spike? HTTP timers plus pool/thread gauges. Only Metaspace class count. Git commit hash from /info. Disk UUID of the container image. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (HTTP timers plus pool/thread gauges.) Q4: /actuator/conditions helps debug? Why auto-config beans appeared or not. Native thread creation in the kernel. G1 region size exclusively. Whether records are on the heap. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Why auto-config beans appeared or not.) Q5: HTTP actuator dead, JVM alive. Next? jcmd from the pod — attach still works. Only retry /heapdump on 8080. Disable GC to free the servlet pool. Restart etcd in the cluster first. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (jcmd from the pod — attach still works.) Q6: High-cardinality userId tags on timers? Dangerous — explodes time series. Required for Micrometer to work. Replaces the need for logs. Forces CGLIB off globally. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Dangerous — explodes time series.) 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 7 · Lesson 9 → · Cheat sheet

lessons.title: WebFlux vs Servlet MVC
lessons.text: 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 8 · Lesson 9 of 9 · ➡️ Capstone Exercise · Cheat sheet WebFlux: Reactive Model vs Servlet MVC ~35 minutes · Module 05 Lesson 9 of 9 · architecture choice, not a Reactor course · builds on S07 , virtual threads Senior Interview Focus: WebFlux is not “faster Spring.” It is an event-loop + non-blocking I/O model. Blocking JDBC on the event loop is an outage. Virtual threads give a second scalability story on the servlet stack. Can you pick MVC+VT vs WebFlux with a decision tree, not a buzzword? Primary sources: Spring WebFlux · Reactive Spring · Boot Reactive Web 1. Why WebFlux Exists Servlet MVC (S07): one thread per in-flight blocking request. High concurrency of slow I/O → huge thread counts, stack memory, context switches. WebFlux: small set of event-loop threads, I/O completion callbacks, many concurrent requests without 1:1 platform threads. Born for gateways, streaming, high fan-out HTTP — if the whole stack is non-blocking . 2. MVC Path request → Tomcat worker │ blocking JDBC / RestTemplate ▼ thread waits (stack allocated the whole time) │ response 3. WebFlux Path request → Netty event loop (N threads, N ≈ cores) │ register I/O, do not block ▼ event-loop free for other connections │ completion → resume Mono/Flux ▼ write response (still on loop or scheduled worker) 4. Event Loops — Blocking Is Fatal Must know: If you call JDBC ResultSet on the event-loop thread, that loop cannot process other connections. One slow query stalls a slice of the server. This is worse than occupying one Tomcat worker — you poison a shared loop. publishOn / bounded elastic schedulers exist to offload blocking — you then have a thread pool again. At that point ask why you aren’t on MVC+VT. 5–7. Mono, Flux, Lazy, Backpressure (Roles Only) Mono — 0..1 value (one JSON body, one user). Flux — 0..N stream (SSE, chunked rows). Lazy: assembling a pipeline does nothing until subscribe (HTTP response subscription). Backpressure: consumer signals demand so a fast publisher doesn’t OOM the heap. Conceptual — not every operator. @GetMapping("/users/{id}") Mono<User> get(@PathVariable String id) { return userRepo.findById(id); // reactive repo — not JPA blocking } 8. MVC vs WebFlux Table Servlet MVC WebFlux Threading Worker per request (or VT) Event loops + workers I/O Blocking OK Non-blocking required on loop Programming Imperative, simple stacks Declarative pipelines, harder dumps Debug Thread dump maps to request Async stacks; need reactor debug / traces Data access JDBC/JPA natural R2DBC / reactive drivers end-to-end Tx @Transactional thread-bound (S06) Different story — don’t paste servlet tx on loop Fit CRUD services, mixed blocking libs Gateway, streams, reactive DB 9. Misconception: “WebFlux Is Always Faster” CPU-bound JSON + business rules: same cores, extra pipeline overhead. Blocking JDBC on WebFlux: slower and less stable than MVC. Benchmark your shape of work. 10. Blocking JDBC on WebFlux JPA/JDBC calls socketRead on whatever thread you ran them. On the event loop = stall. On boundedElastic = hidden Tomcat. Mixing Hibernate Session (thread-bound) with reactive chains is a bug factory. Module 06 will deepen ORM; here: don’t . 11–13. Virtual Threads vs WebFlux Two strategies for “lots of waiting I/O”: MVC + virtual threads — keep imperative style, JDBC, @Transactional; VT unmounts while blocking (pinning caveats, concurrency-0008). WebFlux — keep event loops; every I/O library must be reactive. MVC+VT is simpler for most business services in 2026. WebFlux wins when: streaming, backpressure, reactive clients all the way, gateway routing. 14. Decision Tree Need end-to-end non-blocking + streaming / gateway? YES → WebFlux (and reactive data access) NO → Servlet MVC │ Lots of concurrent blocking I/O, Java 21+? YES → consider spring.threads.virtual.enabled CPU-bound / simple CRUD / JPA? YES → MVC platform threads are fine; measure first Cannot mix starter-web and starter-webflux as two competing servers without a clear choice — Boot picks one web application type. Wrong OnWebApplication conditions (S05) then surprise you. Production Relevance Teams copy a WebFlux template, keep JPA, page the CEO. Thread dumps show event-loop threads in socketRead0 . Fix: move to MVC or extract blocking to a dedicated pool (and accept you lost the model). Interview Articulation “MVC occupies a worker for blocking I/O. WebFlux uses event loops and requires non-blocking I/O; blocking JDBC on the loop is an outage. WebFlux is not automatically faster. For JPA CRUD I pick MVC, and virtual threads if concurrency of blocking calls is the bottleneck. I pick WebFlux when the pipeline is reactive end-to-end.” Senior Interview Questions Why does WebFlux exist if Tomcat already has a pool? What happens if JDBC runs on the Netty loop? Mono vs Flux — one sentence each. Why is the pipeline lazy? Backpressure in one sentence. Is WebFlux always lower latency? VT vs WebFlux — two sentences. @Transactional on a WebFlux handler? When is MVC+VT the senior default? starter-web vs starter-webflux both on the classpath? Revision Notes Event loop ≠ worker pool. Non-blocking all the way or don’t pretend. VT: imperative blocking; WebFlux: reactive I/O. JPA + WebFlux is a smell. Interview One-Liners “WebFlux multiplies concurrency only if I/O doesn’t block the loop.” “Virtual threads scale blocking code; WebFlux scales callbacks.” “Faster is a benchmark, not a stack name.” Senior MCQs Q1: JDBC on the Netty event loop? Stalls that loop — other channels wait. Automatically hops to Tomcat workers. Turns JDBC into R2DBC at runtime. Is required for @Transactional. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Stalls that loop — other channels wait.) Q2: WebFlux always faster than MVC? False — CPU-bound and blocking JDBC disagree. True — event loops beat all CPUs. True if and only if G1 is enabled. True for every JPA findById. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (False — CPU-bound and blocking JDBC disagree.) Q3: Mono represents? At most one asynchronous result. Unbounded platform thread pool. A servlet Filter registration. Hikari’s maximum pool size. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (At most one asynchronous result.) Q4: Typical 2026 CRUD + JPA service default? MVC; consider virtual threads for blocking I/O load. WebFlux plus Hibernate on the event loop. Both starters as two servers always. Skip Tomcat and poll in a while(true). View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (MVC; consider virtual threads for blocking I/O load.) Q5: Virtual threads vs WebFlux? VT scale blocking; WebFlux needs non-blocking I/O. They are identical bytecode after JIT. VT only work inside Flux operators. WebFlux replaces the JVM scheduler. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (VT scale blocking; WebFlux needs non-blocking I/O.) Q6: Assembling a Flux without subscribe? Lazy — no I/O until subscription. Runs immediately on the caller thread. Commits a JDBC transaction always. Registers a Tomcat Filter automatically. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Lazy — no I/O until subscription.) Q7: When WebFlux is the right default? Reactive I/O end-to-end — gateway/streaming. Any service that uses HashMap locally. Whenever Boot version is 3.2+. To avoid writing unit tests. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Reactive I/O end-to-end — gateway/streaming.) Q8: Backpressure is? Consumer demand so publishers don’t flood memory. Tomcat maxThreads divided by two. G1 mixed GC of old regions only. A synonym for HTTP 429 always. View Answer & Explanation Answer: A (Consumer demand so publishers don’t flood memory.) 🏠 Home · ← Lesson 8 · ➡️ Capstone Exercise · Cheat sheet

lessons.title: Capstone Exercise
lessons.text: 🏠 Home · ⬅️ Prev: WebFlux vs MVC Spring Boot Internals Capstone Exercise Capstone exercise • Module 05 • 5 scenarios + 15 interview Qs • optional JUnit • Stub How to use: No new theory. Work scenarios with notes closed. Reveal answers only after you write root cause + fix. Optional: implement the JUnit stub. Tie misses to spring-0001 – 0009 . Scenario Index # Topic Lessons 1 NoSuchBeanDefinitionException S03 S04 2 NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException S04 3 @Transactional ignored S06 4 Auto-config DataSource mystery S05 S08 5 Tomcat 200 / Hikari 20 latency S07 JVM S08 Scenario 1 — NoSuchBeanDefinitionException com.shop.ShopApplication lives in com.shop . A @Service BillingService lives in com.payments.BillingService . Also: shop.billing.enabled=false # application.yml @ConditionalOnProperty(name = "shop.billing.enabled", havingValue = "true") @Component class BillingClient { } Checkout constructor needs BillingClient . Startup: NoSuchBeanDefinitionException: BillingClient . Tasks: root cause (there may be two), discovery path, debug steps, minimal fix. Reveal answer Root cause: (1) com.payments is outside default scan (package of ShopApplication + children). (2) Even if scanned, shop.billing.enabled=false makes @ConditionalOnProperty skip registration. Discovery: Is there a BeanDefinition? /actuator/beans or definition names. Conditions: --debug / /actuator/conditions . Minimal fix: Move billing under com.shop or scanBasePackages = "com.shop", "com.payments" , and set shop.billing.enabled=true in the profile that needs it (or drop the condition). Don’t “fix” with new BillingClient() — you skip the container (S01/S06). Scenario 2 — NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException public interface PaymentGateway { Receipt charge(Money m); } @Service class StripePaymentService implements PaymentGateway {} @Service class RazorpayPaymentService implements PaymentGateway {} @Service class CheckoutService { CheckoutService(PaymentGateway gateway) { } } Tasks: Why it fails. @Primary vs @Qualifier articulation. When List<PaymentGateway> is better. Reveal answer Two beans of type PaymentGateway , injection point unqualified → NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException . @Primary on Stripe = default when a single gateway is requested. @Qualifier("razorpayPaymentService") (default name) on a parameter when that site must be Razorpay. Use both: Primary for most call sites, Qualifier for the exception. List<PaymentGateway> when the use-case is “try all / route by currency” — not a silent pick. Scenario 3 — @Transactional Ignored @Service public class OrderService { @Transactional public void place(PlaceOrder cmd) { repo.save(cmd.toOrder()); this.updateInventory(cmd); // also @Transactional } @Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW) public void updateInventory(PlaceOrder cmd) { ... } } Inventory update rolls back with the outer method; REQUIRES_NEW never starts. Tasks: proxy flow, JDK vs CGLIB, exception rollback, REQUIRES_NEW contrast. Reveal answer this.updateInventory is self-invocation: call stays on the target, never re-enters the Spring proxy, so no new tx, no independent commit. Outer REQUIRED (if place was called via proxy) still wraps save+inventory as one tx. Boot CGLIB class proxy does not rewrite this . Fix: extract InventoryService bean and inject it; or inject self proxy. If updateInventory threw a checked exception without rollbackFor , even a proxied call might commit — separate bug. Scenario 4 — Auto-config DataSource Service A: no user DataSource, starter-jdbc + spring.datasource.url → Hikari appears. Service B: same starter but a @Bean DataSource routingDs() → no second Hikari. Service C: forgot starter → no DataSource, JPA fails. Tasks: dependency → auto-config → conditions → bean. Tools. Reveal answer A: DataSourceAutoConfiguration listed in AutoConfiguration.imports ; OnClass true; OnMissingBean true; properties present → Hikari bean. B: user bean → @ConditionalOnMissingBean(DataSource.class) false → Boot backs off. One pool (yours). C: no JDBC auto-config match (or class missing) → NoSuchBean later. Debug: --debug Condition Evaluation Report, /actuator/conditions . Exclude only if you must disable despite classpath. Scenario 5 — Production Latency Tomcat max=200 , Hikari maximum-pool-size=20 , p99 8s, CPU 15%. Load spike. Tasks: chain; Actuator; metrics; thread dump; JVM tie-in. Reveal answer Most Tomcat workers blocked acquiring a connection or in socketRead on the 20 connections. Raising Tomcat to 800 worsens queues. Measure: Hikari pending, Tomcat busy, HTTP timers (S08). Dump: /threaddump or jcmd Thread.print (JVM S08). Fix: queries, pool vs DB max_connections , timeouts, maybe VT for waiters — not extra workers without extra DB. Virtual threads do not add connections. Senior Interview Round — 15 questions Speak answers first. Then reveal. IoC vs DI in two sentences. Reveal IoC: the container owns create/call graph. DI: collaborators are passed in (usually constructors). DI is a technique inside IoC. What is a bean? Reveal A container-managed object with a BeanDefinition — not every new , not DTOs/entities. ApplicationContext vs BeanFactory. Reveal Context is a BeanFactory plus events, i18n, AOP integration, eager singleton refresh. Lifecycle order: ctor, inject, @PostConstruct, destroy. Reveal Constructor → remaining DI → @PostConstruct / init → (proxy after BPP) → @PreDestroy on close (singletons). Prototype into singleton — 100 HTTP calls. Reveal One prototype unless ObjectProvider or scoped proxy. Default scan base. Reveal Package of @SpringBootApplication and subpackages. @Primary vs @Qualifier. Reveal Primary: default candidate of a type. Qualifier: this injection point’s identity. Qualifier wins locally. Boot 3 auto-config discovery file. Reveal META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports . spring.factories EnableAutoConfiguration key removed in 3.0. User @Bean DataSource — Hikari? Reveal @ConditionalOnMissingBean false → auto-config backs off. Why self-invocation skips @Transactional. Reveal Advice lives on the proxy. this is the target. Default rollback policy. Reveal RuntimeException/Error. Checked commits unless rollbackFor. Filter vs DispatcherServlet. Reveal Filter: servlet chain around the servlet. DispatcherServlet: Spring MVC front controller (mapping, adapters, converters). Liveness vs readiness. Reveal Liveness → restart. Readiness → take traffic. Don’t DB-check liveness. WebFlux + blocking JDBC. Reveal If on the event loop, the loop stalls. Don’t. Use MVC±VT or reactive drivers. Virtual threads vs WebFlux one-liner. Reveal VT scale blocking imperative code; WebFlux scales non-blocking pipelines. Final challenge — 2 minutes Outline aloud: Boot startup → ApplicationContext → BeanDefinitions (scan, @Bean, auto-config + conditions) → instances + lifecycle → AOP proxies / @Transactional → HTTP Tomcat → Filter → DispatcherServlet → Controller → Service → Repo → Actuator for health/metrics. If you skip conditions or proxies, restart the timer. Scoring rubric 90%+ — interview ready for Module 05 internals 75–90% — revise weak letters (usually S05/S06) <75% — re-read those lessons + cheat sheets; re-run scenarios Optional JUnit Copy entire file Open stub Loading… 🏠 Home · ⬅️ Prev: WebFlux vs MVC
